nodes.name: Dual-template MOF@POM assembly
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of MOF@POM involves a dual-template assembly process. First, a CoFe-MOF forms through the self-coordination of Fe³⁺ and Co²⁺ with 1,4-benzenedicarboxylic acid (II), chosen for its layered structure which promotes axial growth and enhances the interaction and stability of POM-Ni-MOF stacking. This formation process is accompanied by the decomposition of symmetric PW₉-Ni₄ into a trilacunary Keggin anion, [PW₉O₃₄]⁹⁻ (PW₉). Subsequently, the CoFe-MOF reassembles with PW₉, facilitated by the Ni-O bridge, to form the innovative MOF@POM superstructure.

nodes.source_text: The synthesis of MOF@POM involves a dual-template assembly process (fig. S1). First, a CoFeMOF forms through the self-coordination of Fe^{3+} and Co^{2+} with 1,4-benzenedicarboxylic acid (II)... to form the innovative MOF@POM superstructure (Fig. 1A).

nodes.description: OER performance via cyclic voltammetry in alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements reveal the exceptional activity of MOF@POM for water oxidation ... optimized MOF@POM demonstrates a very low overpotential of only 178 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm^{-2} ... Tafel slopes ... 27.7 mV dec^{-1} ... TOF of Co and Fe in MOF@POM is 78 times higher ... mass activity of MOF@POM is >7 times greater ... MOF@POM has the lowest charge-transfer resistance ... electrical conductivity of MOF@POM is higher ... negligible degradation for 1000 hours at a current density of 100 mA cm^{-2}

At 25°C, a current density of 1 A cm^{-2} is achieved with a cell voltage of only 1.83 V for MOF@POM ... 1.78 V is sufficient to achieve a current density of 3 A cm^{-2} ... maintains a current density of 2 A cm^{-2} for 5140 hours with a minimal decay rate of 0.02 mV h^{-1}

nodes.description: AEMWE performance at 80°C in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Even under simulated real-world operation conditions (1 M KOH, 60° to 80°C), MOF@POM displays exceptional activity, achieving a current density of 2 A cm^{-2} with a very efficient cell voltage of only 1.69 V at 80°C ... Increasing the cell voltage to 2.0 V enables a current density exceeding 5.5 A cm^{-2}
The MOF@POM cell shows a decay rate of only 0.015 mV h^{-1} after 2000 hours of operation at 1 A cm^{-2}

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images display a petal-like morphology for MOF@POM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images display a petal-like morphology for MOF@POM (Fig. 1B)

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms monolayer thickness of 3.54 ± 0.18 nm for MOF@POM vs 1.73 ± 0.17 nm for pure MOF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurements confirm a monolayer thickness of 3.54 ± 0.18 nm for MOF@POM (Fig. 1C), in contrast to the pure MOF monolayer thickness of 1.73 ± 0.17 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: Spherical aberration-corrected TEM reveals thin lamellar structures of MOF@POM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveals thin lamellar structures (fig. S6)

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images with SAED show crystalline facets in MOF@POM with 0.63 nm spacing, consistent with pure MOF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images, coupled with selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns (Fig. 1D), highlight the crystalline facets within the MOF@POM, with a crystalline spacing of 0.63 nm, consistent with the pure MOF

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD results corroborate the (200) and (001) facets for the MIL-53 MOF within MOF@POM superstructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) results corroborate this observation of the (200) and (001) facets for the MIL-53 MOF (fig. S8)

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR spectroscopy validates characteristic absorption peaks of PW9 within MOF@POM superstructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy also validates the presence of characteristic absorption peaks of PW9 within the MOF@POM superstructure (fig. S9)

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM with elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Co, Fe, Ni, C, O, P, and W within MOF@POM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy analysis of MOF@POM, coupled with elemental mapping (fig. S11 and table S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: Full-range synchrotron PDF analysis confirms MOF@POM superstructure with excellent fit (R²≈0.88).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Full-range synchrotron pair distribution function (PDF) analysis provides a detailed view of the atomic structure of MOF@POM (fig. S12)

nodes.characterization_summary: Partial-PDF analysis shows excellent agreement between theoretical and experimental Ni-Fe distances in MOF@POM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Partial-PDF (p-PDF) analysis further characterized the MOF@POM structure

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows MOF@POM-act transitions from initial MOF state to mixed MOF/hydroxide state forming CoFe-related metal (oxy)hydroxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD characterization corroborates these observations, showing that the MOF@POM structure transitions from its initial state to a mixed state of MOF and hydroxide, ultimately forming the desired CoFe-related metal (oxy)hydroxides (Fig. 3A and fig. S41)

properties.description: High crystallinity indicated by sharp peaks

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows organic peaks at 1611, 1422, 633, 376 cm⁻¹ diminish at 1.53 V vs RHE, replaced by 540-465 cm⁻¹ peaks indicating hydroxyl oxide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy provides real-time insights into surface structure changes... characteristic Raman peaks associated with organic components at 1611, 1422, 633, and 376 cm⁻¹ diminish. At a potential of 1.53 V versus RHE, these peaks nearly disappear, replaced by new peaks (540 to 465 cm⁻¹)

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of MOF@POM-act shows new O 1s peak for M-OH and increased valence states for Co and Fe, confirming conversion to metal (oxy)hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This phenomenon was further corroborated by x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy of MOF-act and MOF@POM-act after the stability test (figs. S46 and S47)

nodes.characterization_summary: PDF analysis of MOF@POM-act demonstrates excellent alignment with structural model.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The detected PDF of MOF@POM-act demonstrates excellent alignment with the model presented in Fig. 3C (fig. S48)

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES shows rapid increase in valence states of Co and Fe sites with applied potential; Ni shows less pronounced change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The x-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectrum (Fig. 3D and fig. S50) shows a rapid increase in the valence states of the Co and Fe sites

properties.description: Dark blue curve with sharp peak

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows Co and Fe coordination environments transition from M-O to M-OH to M-OOH with bond length ~1.9 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended x-ray absorption fine structure analysis (Fig. 3D and fig. S52) indicates that the coordination environments of Co and Fe transition from M-O ... to M-OOH
